s.g: Suffix used to form nouns, often colloquial and endearing, from nouns or adjectives. Sometimes a new meaning is imparted.
crimson, purple (deep, bluish shade of red)
a military rank in Russia (18-19 centuries)
really!; really and truly!; honest to God!
Zhmerynka (a city, the administrative center of Zhmerynka Raion, Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine)
yellow and blue (the colors of the Ukrainian flag)
Ukrainian (relating to Ukrainian authorities, the Ukrainian national team, etc.)
bewitched, enchanted, spellbound (of a person; experiencing being enchanted or bewitched)
bewitched, enchanted, spellbound (of a look, one's eyes, etc.; expressing being enchanted or bewitched)
to become interested, to take an interest
same to you (I wish to you what you have just wished to me)
mass media (public communication that reaches a large audience)
the same, one and the same
the same one(s), one and the same
to take away (by vehicle), to drive away, to take (someone or something by vehicle)
to press (for), to push (for), to struggle (for), to win, to bring off, to put across
to learn, to hear from rumors
signalman, signaller; postal / telecommunications worker, communication man
evil eye, hex, jinx, whammy (an evil spell)
